newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka sees no rise in 1997 defence budget.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka sees no rise in 1997 defence budget.

text.p: Sri Lanka, waging a protracted war against Tamil Tiger rebels, does not expect a rise in defence spending this year, a top finance ministry official said on Wednesday.
P.B. Jayasundera, deputy secretary of treasury, said military spending should not top the proposed budget of 44 billion rupees ($758.6 million) for 1997.
"The 1997 budget is more a military type of budget, which has fully accommodated the military requirement," he said.
"Each plane crash does not mean that we have to add something," Jayasundera said in reference to the tiny air force, which has lost six aircraft in operations against the rebels this year.
Sri Lanka's defence spending in 1995 was 34 billion rupees, but rose sharply to nearly 46 billion, or about six percent of gross domestic product, last year as the war escalated.
Jayasundera said the big increase was largely because previous budget forecasts had been made on the assumption that there would be no escalation in the conflict.
"There was a gross underestimation in terms of events," he said.
The People's Alliance government of President Chandrika Kumaratunga, which won power in 1994, promptly launched peace negotiations with the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels.
The LTTE, fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in the north and east, unilaterally broke off the talks in April 1995 when they attacked a Navy ship in the eastern port of Trincomalee.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed since the war began in 1983. The LTTE says the number is higher. ($1 = 58 rupees)
